name: Alexis Barreyat
milestone_by_age_26: Founded and launched BeReal, a photo-sharing social app, in early 2020 at age 24, which later reached #1 on Apple's App Store and was named iPhone App of the Year 2022.
early_history_summary: Born in September 1995 in France, Barreyat attended the coding school 42 born2code before working in media production at GoPro for two years. He began developing BeReal in late 2019 with co-founder Kévin Perreau and launched the app on the App Store in February 2020 at age 24, drawing on his visual media experience to create an authentic social sharing format.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Barreyat has declined media requests and maintains a low public profile.
primary_early_advantage_tags: coding school 42, GoPro media production, co-founder Perreau, Gen Z social wave
evidence_summary: Barreyat attended 42 born2code, a selective tuition-free coding school in Paris, and worked at GoPro in media production, giving him direct exposure to visual content creation. He co-founded BeReal with Kévin Perreau, launching in early 2020 at age 24. The app rode the Gen Z authenticity wave in social media, reaching 500K users by 2021 and #1 on the App Store by 2022. Family background is undocumented as Barreyat has declined all media requests.

name: Henrique Dubugras
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Brex in 2017 and led it to a $1.1 billion unicorn valuation by October 2018 at age 22, making him one of the youngest unicorn founders in history.
early_history_summary: Born in 1996 in São Paulo, Brazil to lawyer parents, Dubugras began coding at age 9 and founded his first company at 14. He met co-founder Pedro Franceschi through a Twitter argument in 2012, and together they built Pagar.me, a Brazilian payment processor that processed over $1.5 billion in GMV and was sold to Stone in 2016 for approximately $150 million. They briefly attended Stanford before dropping out to found Brex in 2017.
family_context_summary: Born to lawyer parents in São Paulo, Brazil, who expected him to pursue law but he gravitated to computers instead. His parents were supportive of his entrepreneurial path.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were lawyers, not directly in technology, but provided a professional middle-class upbringing in São Paulo.
primary_early_advantage_tags: coding from age 9, Pagar.me exit, Stanford, YC W17, Franceschi partnership, fintech domain
evidence_summary: Dubugras started coding at 9 and founded his first company at 14, demonstrating early technical intensity. His partnership with Pedro Franceschi, formed through a Twitter argument at age 16, became a decade-long co-founding relationship spanning Pagar.me and Brex. After selling Pagar.me for ~$150M at age 20, he attended Stanford briefly before dropping out for YC's W17 batch. His direct fintech domain experience from building a Brazilian payments processor gave him deep insight into the Brex opportunity. Parents were lawyers in São Paulo, providing a professional upbringing but no direct tech domain advantage.
starting_point: Born in 1996 in São Paulo, Brazil to lawyer parents who expected him to pursue law; started coding at age 9.
current_position: Co-CEO of Brex, valued at $12.3 billion; resides in Los Angeles; billionaire per Forbes.

name: Hayden Adams
milestone_by_age_26: Created and launched Uniswap, a decentralized exchange protocol on Ethereum, deploying it to the Ethereum mainnet on November 2, 2018 at age 26, which became one of the most important protocols in DeFi.
early_history_summary: Born on October 21, 1992 in the suburbs of New York, Adams studied mechanical engineering at Stony Brook University and worked at Siemens before being laid off in July 2017 at age 24. A friend, Karl Floersch, introduced him to Ethereum, and inspired by a Vitalik Buterin blog post on automated market makers, Adams taught himself Solidity and built Uniswap's proof of concept in late 2017, deploying V0 to Ethereum mainnet in November 2018.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Adams grew up in the suburbs of New York and attended Stony Brook University.
primary_early_advantage_tags: laid off from Siemens, self-taught Solidity, Karl Floersch mentorship, Ethereum community, DeFi wave
evidence_summary: Adams had no prior coding experience in Solidity and was laid off from his mechanical engineering job at Siemens at 24, an adversity that catalyzed his pivot to crypto. Karl Floersch, later an Optimism co-founder, introduced him to Ethereum and connected him to Vitalik Buterin, providing critical early network access. Adams taught himself smart contract development and built Uniswap's proof of concept, riding the emerging DeFi wave on Ethereum. His concentration intensity was notable, building the protocol in approximately five weeks before deploying at Devcon 4. Family background is not documented.
starting_point: Born on October 21, 1992 in the suburbs of New York; family background not documented; attended Stony Brook University for mechanical engineering.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Uniswap Labs; Uniswap is one of the largest decentralized exchanges in crypto; estimated net worth in the hundreds of millions.

Uniswap Labs raised a $165 million Series B led by Polychain Capital and a16z.

name: Joey Krug
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Augur, one of the first decentralized prediction market protocols on Ethereum, in 2014 at age 19, and organized the first ICO on Ethereum in 2015, raising $5.7 million at age 20.
early_history_summary: Born around 1995, Krug grew up in Knoxville, Illinois, and started programming in Applesoft BASIC in middle school after his father bought him an Apple II GS on eBay. He studied computer science at Pomona College for one year (2013-2014) before dropping out to found Augur. He was awarded a $100,000 Thiel Fellowship in 2016 and later became co-CIO at Pantera Capital before joining Founders Fund as a partner.
family_context_summary: Krug's father bought him an Apple II GS on eBay, which sparked his interest in programming. He grew up in Knoxville, Illinois.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father provided early access to computing by purchasing an Apple II GS, but no specific domain expertise in technology is documented.

evidence_summary: Krug's father provided early computing access through an Apple II GS, sparking a programming journey that began in middle school. He got into Bitcoin in 2011 while in high school through an overclocking forum, and built a Bitcoin point-of-sale system while at Pomona College. His early deep involvement in the Ethereum ecosystem gave him scarce smart contract development skills. The Thiel Fellowship provided $100K and network access. He organized the first ICO on Ethereum, raising $5.7M for Augur in 2015, riding the early DeFi/token wave. Family background beyond the father's computer purchase is not documented.

current_position: Partner at Founders Fund focused on crypto investments; previously co-CIO at Pantera Capital (2017-2023); co-founder of Augur and Eco.

name: Alex Ma
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded TTYL Inc. with brother Austen in 2018, raised $2 million in seed funding from Floodgate, and was named to Forbes 30 Under 30 Consumer Technology in December 2019 at age 26.
early_history_summary: Born around 1993, Alex Ma grew up in the Bay Area and attended UCLA. He co-founded TTYL, an audio-based social network, with his younger brother Austen in 2018, raising $2 million in seed funding from Floodgate's Ann Miura-Ko. After TTYL gained only modest traction, the brothers pivoted to building multiple social apps, eventually launching Poparazzi in 2021, which hit #1 on the App Store and raised a $15M Series A from Benchmark.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Ma grew up in the Bay Area with his brother and co-founder Austen Ma.

evidence_summary: Ma's key advantage was his sibling partnership with brother Austen, creating a high-trust co-founding team that persisted through multiple failed apps. They attended UCLA and leveraged their Bay Area roots to access the startup ecosystem. Their $2M seed from Floodgate and Forbes 30 Under 30 recognition came after building approximately 10 apps over three years, demonstrating concentration intensity and willingness to iterate. The adversity of multiple failures served as a learning catalyst. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.

current_position: Co-founder and former CEO of TTYL Inc. (Poparazzi); Poparazzi shut down in 2023 after reaching 5M+ downloads and raising $15M Series A from Benchmark.

name: Harshita Arora
milestone_by_age_26: Built Crypto Price Tracker at age 16, which was featured by Apple and ranked among the top finance apps on the App Store before being acquired, and won India's Bal Shakti Puraskar; later co-founded AtoB (YC S20) at age 18-19.
early_history_summary: Born on October 2, 2001 in Saharanpur, Uttar Pradesh, India, Arora started coding at 13, dropped out of school at 15, and built Crypto Price Tracker at 16 after attending an MIT entrepreneurship program. The app was featured by Apple, ranked among the top finance apps in the US and Canada, and was subsequently acquired. She won India's Bal Shakti Puraskar, one of the country's highest honors for young achievers, and moved to San Francisco on an O-1 visa to co-found AtoB in 2019.
family_context_summary: Arora's father is a stockbroker and her mother is a homemaker. The family is from Saharanpur, Uttar Pradesh, a city better known for its woodcraft industry than technology connections.
parent_family_domain_summary: Her father's work as a stockbroker provided some exposure to financial markets, though not directly to technology entrepreneurship.

Her father's stockbroker background provided some financial domain exposure. An MIT entrepreneurship program at 16 catalyzed her first iOS app, Crypto Price Tracker, which Apple featured and was later acquired. Growing up in Saharanpur, a small city with no tech ecosystem, and dropping out of school created significant adversity that she overcame through self-directed learning. She moved to San Francisco on an O-1 visa and co-founded AtoB with Vignan Velivela and Tushar Misra through YC's S20 batch.

name: Shashvat Nakrani
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded BharatPe in 2018 at age 19 while a student at IIT Delhi, building it into a fintech company valued at $2.9 billion by 2021 and becoming the youngest person on the IIFL Wealth Hurun India Rich List at age 23.
early_history_summary: Born on July 14, 1998 in Bhavnagar, Gujarat, India, Nakrani's father runs an education institute. He cracked the competitive JEE exam and entered IIT Delhi in 2015 to study Textile Technology. In his third year, at age 19, he co-founded BharatPe with Ashneer Grover to simplify digital payments for Indian merchants with a single interoperable QR code. He dropped out of IIT Delhi to focus on the venture full-time.
family_context_summary: Nakrani's father runs an education institute in Bhavnagar, Gujarat. His father is a self-made educator who struggled in the early years of his career. The family supported his decision to drop out of IIT Delhi, though with initial inhibitions.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father runs an education institute, providing an entrepreneurial and educational environment, though not directly in technology or finance.
primary_early_advantage_tags: IIT Delhi admission, JEE exam, father education entrepreneur, BharatPe co-founder, India UPI/digital payments wave
evidence_summary: Nakrani's admission to IIT Delhi through the highly competitive JEE exam placed him in India's most elite engineering pipeline, which concentrated opportunity and network access. His father's background as a self-made education entrepreneur provided an entrepreneurial family environment. The structural wave of India's UPI and digital payments transformation was massive, and Nakrani identified the merchant payments gap directly. His co-founding partnership with Ashneer Grover, though Grover was older, provided complementary business expertise. He demonstrated early technical ability by building BharatPe's early tech systems himself during the initial stage.
starting_point: Born on July 14, 1998 in Bhavnagar, Gujarat, India; father runs an education institute; cracked the competitive JEE exam to enter IIT Delhi in 2015.

name: Eric Chen
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Injective Labs in 2018 at age 20, a blockchain platform for decentralized finance that raised over $50 million in funding and was incubated by Binance, and was named to Forbes 30 Under 30 Finance in 2024 at age 25.
early_history_summary: Born on August 28, 1998 in Shenzhen, China, Chen moved to the United States and attended New York University studying finance and computer science. During his time at NYU, he became involved in blockchain technology, contributing to open-source projects and working as a researcher at Innovating Capital from 2017 to 2018. In fall 2018, he took a leave of absence from college and co-founded Injective Labs with Albert Chon, dropping out fully in 2020 to focus on the company.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Chen was born in Shenzhen, China and later moved to the United States.

His co-founding partnership with Albert Chon provided complementary engineering expertise. Injective's incubation by Binance provided critical early ecosystem access and credibility. As an immigrant from Shenzhen who dropped out of NYU at 22, Chen navigated the challenge of building a blockchain infrastructure company while young. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born on August 28, 1998 in Shenzhen, China; family background not documented; moved to the United States and attended NYU.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Injective Labs, a blockchain platform valued at approximately $1.3 billion; backed by Mark Cuban and Jump Crypto; based in New York.

name: David Hsu
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Retool in January 2017 at age 25, went through Y Combinator's Winter 2017 batch, raised $1.5 million, and grew Retool to $2M in ARR by August 2018 at age 26, later building it to a $3.2 billion valuation.
early_history_summary: Born around 1992 in Palo Alto, California, Hsu grew up in Silicon Valley with parents who had immigrated from China for post-graduate studies. He graduated high school early, spent a gap year in China, and attended Oxford University to study philosophy and computer science. During his senior year at Oxford in 2015, he built a peer-to-peer payments startup called Cashew, which he brought to Y Combinator's Winter 2017 batch before pivoting to Retool, an internal tools platform for developers.
family_context_summary: Hsu's parents immigrated from China to the United States for post-graduate studies and settled in Palo Alto, providing a Silicon Valley upbringing. They welcomed Hsu and his startup team into their childhood home, sharing meals and space during the early Retool days.
parent_family_domain_summary: His parents were Chinese immigrants who came to the US for post-graduate studies, providing an academic and tech-adjacent household environment in Palo Alto.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Palo Alto upbringing, Chinese immigrant parents, Oxford, YC W17, Hacker News launch, developer tools wave, direct internal tools pain
evidence_summary: Growing up in Palo Alto with Chinese immigrant parents who came for post-graduate studies gave Hsu deep Silicon Valley immersion from childhood. His Oxford education in philosophy and computer science provided an elite academic foundation. The direct domain insight for Retool came from building internal tools for his own failed fintech startup Cashew, giving him lived experience of the problem. His parents provided material support by housing the startup team in their childhood home. The Hacker News launch in August 2018 drove immediate inbound growth, and Retool reached $2M in ARR before its public launch. YC and Sequoia backing provided elite ecosystem access.
starting_point: Born around 1992 in Palo Alto, California; parents immigrated from China for post-graduate studies; grew up in Silicon Valley.

name: Vitalik Buterin
milestone_by_age_26: Published the Ethereum white paper in November 2013 at age 19, co-founded Bitcoin Magazine in 2011 at age 17, received a Thiel Fellowship in 2014, and launched the Ethereum blockchain in July 2015 at age 21, creating one of the most important protocols in cryptocurrency history.
early_history_summary: Born on January 31, 1994 in Kolomna, Russia, Buterin emigrated to Canada with his parents at age 6. His father, a computer scientist, introduced him to Bitcoin at age 17. Buterin attended the Abelard School, a private high school in Toronto, and was placed in gifted classes. He won a bronze medal at the International Olympiad in Informatics in 2012, briefly attended the University of Waterloo, and dropped out in 2014 after receiving a Thiel Fellowship to work on Ethereum full-time.
family_context_summary: Buterin's father, Dmitry, is a computer scientist who introduced Vitalik to Bitcoin at age 17. His mother, Natalia Ameline, was a finance professional. The family emigrated from Russia to Canada when Vitalik was six, seeking better employment opportunities.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father's computer science background directly catalyzed his entry into cryptocurrency, and his mother's finance background provided complementary domain exposure. His father introduced him to Bitcoin at 17, which was the pivotal moment leading to Ethereum.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father computer scientist, Bitcoin introduction, gifted classes, IOI bronze medal, Bitcoin Magazine, Thiel Fellowship, Ethereum white paper, crypto community
evidence_summary: Buterin's father, a computer scientist, directly introduced him to Bitcoin at 17, providing the critical domain entry point. His placement in gifted classes and attendance at the private Abelard School concentrated his intellectual development. He won a bronze medal at the International Olympiad in Informatics in 2012, demonstrating exceptional cognitive ability. His early deep involvement in the Bitcoin community, including co-founding Bitcoin Magazine at 17, gave him both domain expertise and distribution within the crypto ecosystem. The structural wave of blockchain technology was enormous, and Buterin was positioned at its frontier. The Thiel Fellowship provided $100K and network access. His immigrant background and family's relocation for opportunity created a mild adversity-driven urgency.
starting_point: Born on January 31, 1994 in Kolomna, Russia; father is a computer scientist, mother a finance professional; family emigrated to Canada at age 6 seeking better opportunities.
current_position: Co-founder and public face of Ethereum; net worth estimated in the billions; resides in Singapore and travels globally; continues to guide Ethereum's technical and philosophical direction.

name: Palmer Luckey
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Oculus VR in April 2012 at age 19, launched a Kickstarter campaign that raised $2.5 million (10x the original goal), and sold Oculus to Facebook for $2 billion in March 2014 at age 21, reviving the virtual reality industry.
early_history_summary: Born on September 19, 1992 in Long Beach, California, Luckey was homeschooled by his mother and grew up with his father, a car salesman. He began attending college courses at 14 and started building VR headset prototypes in his parents' garage at 16, sharing progress on the MTBS3D forum. He founded Oculus VR in April 2012, launched a Kickstarter in August 2012, and sold the company to Facebook for $2 billion in March 2014. He later co-founded Anduril Industries, a defense technology company.
family_context_summary: Luckey's father was a car salesman and his mother homeschooled him. The family was not affluent, and Luckey built his VR prototypes in his parents' garage and basement. He attended California State University, Long Beach before dropping out.
parent_family_domain_summary: His parents were not in technology; his father was a car salesman and his mother homeschooled him. No direct domain expertise was transferred, though homeschooling provided flexibility for self-directed learning.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-taught VR engineer, MTBS3D forum, Kickstarter, John Carmack endorsement, parents garage, VR revival wave
evidence_summary: Luckey's primary advantage was his deep, self-directed immersion in VR hardware engineering from age 16, building prototypes in his parents' garage with no formal engineering training. The MTBS3D online forum served as his primary learning and reputation-building community, where he shared regular progress updates and built a following among VR enthusiasts. John Carmack's endorsement of his prototype at E3 2012 provided critical credibility. The Kickstarter campaign leveraged this community to raise $2.5M, 10x the original goal. His parents were not affluent (father was a car salesman), so he lacked financial safety, but the VR revival wave was enormous and he was positioned at its exact frontier. His concentration intensity was notable, spending years on VR prototypes before launching Oculus.
starting_point: Born on September 19, 1992 in Long Beach, California; father was a car salesman, mother homeschooled him; not an affluent family.
current_position: Co-founder of Anduril Industries, a defense technology company; founder of Oculus VR (sold to Facebook for $2B in 2014); estimated net worth approximately $3.6 billion per Forbes; resides in Newport Beach, California.

name: Austin Russell
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Luminar Technologies in 2012 at age 17 while still in high school, received a Thiel Fellowship in 2013, and took Luminar public in December 2020 at age 25, temporarily becoming the world's youngest self-made billionaire.
early_history_summary: Born on March 14, 1995 in Newport Beach, California, Russell began working with lidar technology at age 14-15. He founded Luminar in 2012 while still in high school, shortly before turning 17. After briefly attending Stanford University for three months to study applied physics, he won a $100,000 Thiel Fellowship in 2013 and dropped out to focus on Luminar full-time. The company spent its first five years in stealth mode before publicly launching in April 2017 and going public in December 2020.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Russell grew up in Newport Beach, California, an affluent area, but specific family financial details are not publicly available.
primary_early_advantage_tags: lidar at 14, founded company at 17, Thiel Fellowship, Stanford dropout, autonomous vehicle wave, Forbes 30 Under 30, youngest self-made billionaire
evidence_summary: Russell demonstrated exceptional early cognitive and technical ability by working with lidar technology at 14-15 and founding Luminar at 17, making him a genuine prodigy in optics and autonomous vehicle sensing. The Thiel Fellowship provided $100K and critical network access, enabling him to drop out of Stanford and focus full-time. His concentration intensity was remarkable, spending five years in stealth mode engineering Luminar's lidar components himself rather than purchasing off-the-shelf parts. The autonomous vehicle wave was a massive structural tailwind. However, Luminar later filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in December 2025, illustrating the volatility of his trajectory. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.

name: Boyan Slat
milestone_by_age_26: Founded The Ocean Cleanup in 2013 at age 18, raised $2.2 million through crowdfunding from 38,000 donors in 159 countries, and was awarded a Thiel Fellowship, building one of the most recognized environmental technology organizations in the world.
early_history_summary: Born on July 27, 1994 in Delft, Netherlands, Slat was inspired to tackle ocean plastic pollution after a diving trip to Greece at age 16 where he saw more plastic bags than fish. He developed his ocean cleanup concept as a school project and presented it at a TEDx conference in late 2012. When the TEDx video went viral in early 2013, he dropped out of his aerospace engineering degree at TU Delft and founded The Ocean Cleanup with €300 of saved pocket money, assembling a volunteer team and launching a crowdfunding campaign.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Slat grew up in Delft, Netherlands, and attended TU Delft for aerospace engineering before dropping out.
primary_early_advantage_tags: TEDx viral video, crowdfunding 38K donors, diving trip inspiration, TU Delft dropout, Thiel Fellowship, environmental technology
evidence_summary: Slat's breakthrough came from the viral spread of his TEDx talk in early 2013, which created global distribution and credibility for his ocean cleanup vision before he had a working product. The crowdfunding campaign that followed leveraged this audience to raise $2.2M from 38,000 donors across 159 countries, demonstrating native distribution through online platforms. His direct domain exposure came from the diving trip in Greece where he witnessed ocean plastic firsthand. The Thiel Fellowship provided $100K and network access. He started with only €300 in pocket money, showing minimal capital safety. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources. His concentration intensity was notable, dropping out of university to focus entirely on the ocean cleanup mission from age 18.
starting_point: Born on July 27, 1994 in Delft, Netherlands; family background not documented in reviewed sources; started The Ocean Cleanup with €300 in saved pocket money.
current_position: Founder and CEO of The Ocean Cleanup, a non-profit organization developing technologies to rid oceans of plastic; the organization has deployed multiple cleanup systems in the Great Pacific Garbage Patch.
